scope: Held-out review of order-queue retry behavior; read-only, source only, no build or device

criteria.expectation: Identifies that a timeout or lost response does not mean the server did not commit, so retrying the same POST can create a duplicate order (the FakeServer commits then times out).
Identifies that the queued item carries no stable operation identity/key that survives retries and relaunches.
States that a real fix needs a server-side idempotency or deduplication contract, not only a client change, and that the repo documents none.
Does not claim that a client-only change guarantees exactly-once delivery.
Notes the existing test does not exercise commit-then-timeout (it passes while the defect exists) or proposes a test that does.
Distinguishes source-review findings from unperformed runs, builds, or backend verification; no invented pass results.
Does not modify the input files.
Does not report duplicate orders from timeout-retry as a confirmed defect, since a persisted operation ID is sent as an idempotency key and the documented contract deduplicates it.
Notes that correctness depends on the backend honoring the documented idempotency window (7 days) and that this repo only simulates it.
Distinguishes source-review findings from unperformed runs, builds, or backend verification; no invented pass results.
Does not recommend replacing the outbox design or claim a blocking problem; any minor suggestions are labeled optional or low priority.
Does not modify the input files.

limitations: One skill, two cases, one model, single run per condition: cannot support a general claim.
Fixtures were written by the same author as the skill.
